document_title: Seven of 254, Alaska's Rural Health AI
post_copy:
Alaska's seven rural health AI awards total less than one robotic surgery award in Ketchikan.

About $5.4 million for the seven. About $7 million for the one. Both preliminary. Robotic surgery isn't AI.

The largest of the seven is the Alaska Stroke Coalition's $3,156,626 imaging network across 21 acute care hospitals its award never names. Three AI awards filed "Statewide" hold about $4.5 million. Seven of 254 Year 1 awards. About two cents a dollar.

CMS awarded Alaska $272,653,149 for Year 2 on November 9th, second only to Texas. The state health department plans a dashboard of every award by year end.

A blister web holds all 254 Year 1 awards at one scale with the seven AI awards in gold. A table gives their aims and a map shows where the AI money is filed.

How many of the 21 hospitals will the year-end dashboard name?

#AlaskaHealthPolicy #StrokeCare #HealthIT

slides.headline: Two read the body. Three write the chart.
slides.body: The stroke network reads scans and Mat-Su Regional's headband reads brain waves. Maniilaq, Ptarmigan and Kodiak use AI to write clinical notes. MapHabit maps daily routines and the Independent Living Council sizes up assistive tech.

slides.body: Two cloud platforms run on the hospitals' existing image systems, with no new imaging hardware. They also flag bleeds, lung clots, and aortic and spinal injury.

Year 1 amounts are the state's preliminary notices of intent to award, projected as of October 9th, and may still be adjusted. The AI count is the seven awards whose titles or summaries name an AI tool, so a project that uses AI without saying so would be missed, which is why the deck says at least. The Ketchikan figure is the workbook's preliminary $6,967,728, and CMS cited $6.5 million in August for the first robotic assisted surgeries in Southern Southeast Alaska.
aftercare: Post Tuesday to Thursday between 8 and 11 a.m. Alaska time, the strongest slots. The next one is Tuesday, November 10th. Drafts arrive daily and you own the cadence.
Paste the first comment within 60 seconds of posting.
Reply to every comment in the first 60 to 90 minutes. Keep every Year 1 figure called preliminary and keep the AI count described as at least seven.

Likely question, why isn't Ketchikan's robot counted as AI? Suggested reply. The count takes only the awards whose titles or summaries say they buy or build an AI tool. Ketchikan's about $7 million preliminary award buys robotic-assisted surgery and isn't one of them, which is why the deck sets it beside the seven rather than among them.

Likely question, which 21 hospitals? Suggested reply. Neither the award summary nor CMS's August release names them, only the count of 21 acute care hospitals. The state's planned year-end dashboard is the natural place for that list.

Likely question, is two cents a dollar too little or too much? Suggested reply. The deck takes no side on the amount. Its ask is that the state's dashboard report each of the seven stated aims, so the question can be answered with results rather than guesses.

Watch the Alaska Department of Health's rural health page (health.alaska.gov/en/education/rural-health-transformation-program/) for the dashboard the state plans by year end. If it appears, check whether it names the 21 hospitals and answer the caption's question in a reply rather than editing the post.
Note saves and comments at 48 hours.
editor_notes_for_email: UPDATE, not a repeat. No.35, No.45 and No.59 covered this program more than 30 days ago. New since then are CMS's November 9th Year 2 award ($272,653,149, second only to Texas), the closed Year 1 list of 254 awards and the Year 2 rules that weigh progress, including ways to measure results. AI COUNT. The seven are the Year 1 awards whose titles or summaries say they buy or build an AI tool, summed from the state's preliminary workbook. A project that uses AI without saying so would be missed, so the deck says at least. Bartlett's EHR conversion mentions AI only as something its old systems can't reach and is not counted. CAPTION ROOM. It needed its one extra round before it passed.
